name: White-tailed Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Southern mexico (sierra madre del sur from guerrero to western oaxaca)
description: Rather local but distinctive, medium-sized hummingbird found in foothills of the Sierra Madre del Sur in Guerrero, Mexico; endemic. Favors humid evergreen forest and shade-coffee plantations.

name: Rufous-tailed Antbird
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (southeastern minas gerais, southern espírito santo, and rio de janeiro)
description: Medium-sized antbird with a long rusty tail and rusty wings. Found in the understory of dense humid forests with bamboo.

name: Sierra Madre Ground-Warbler
rangeDescription: Northeastern luzon (philippines)
description: A medium-sized bird of the forest floor from the lowlands to low elevations in the mountains in northeastern Luzon. Fairly stout, with a pale lower bill, long legs, and large feet.

name: Bridled Sparrow
rangeDescription: Arid central plateau of mexico (puebla to oaxaca)
description: Very handsome but rather local sparrow endemic to interior southern Mexico. Found in scrubby oak woodland and brushy cactus scrub of dry tropical foothills and interior valleys.

name: Kaempfer's Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Eastern brazil (western piauí)
description: Visually striking woodpecker. Has a chestnut head and flight feathers, and is otherwise creamy yellow with a black chest and spots on the wings and back.

name: Silvery-cheeked Hornbill
rangeDescription: Montane and coastal forest of ethiopia to southern mozambique
description: Big, spectacular, black-and-white hornbill. Both sexes show a pale bill, with a large casque that is larger in males and smaller in females.

name: Kashmir Nuthatch
rangeDescription: Mountains of northeastern afghanistan to northern pakistan, northwestern india, and northwestern nepal
description: Unremarkable-looking nuthatch with a highly restricted range. Found in hill and montane forests; favors coniferous-dominated forest types.

name: Mountain Yellow-Warbler
rangeDescription: Southern south sudan, mountains of eastern democratic republic of the congo, northeastern uganda, kenya, rwanda, burundi, tanzania, and northern malawi
description: Medium-sized, long-tailed, long-billed warbler. The back is olive-green and the underparts yellow.

name: Rusty-cheeked Hornbill
rangeDescription: Southern myanmar and southeastern thailand
description: Brownish, medium-sized hornbill. Male is dusty brown above and rusty-colored below, with a pale bill and blue-gray skin around the eye.

name: Purplish-mantled Tanager
rangeDescription: Humid western andes of colombia and northwestern ecuador
description: Fairly small, chunky tanager with stout bill. Almost entirely blue, darker indigo on head, paler cerulean towards tail.

name: Perija Metaltail
rangeDescription: Sierra de perijá (colombia/venezuela border)
description: Small, short-billed hummingbird found only in the Perijá Mountains, which straddle the border between Colombia and Venezuela. Similar to the more common Tyrian Metalail, but larger with a longer coppery (not bluish) tail; male is also darker and female has speckles on the throat.

name: Chestnut-rumped Thornbill
rangeDescription: Arid and semiarid interior of southern australia; to coast in west
description: Small bird with thin pointed bill, found in woodland and shrubland across much of arid inland temperate Australia. Brownish gray above, cream-colored below, with white eye, pale speckling on forecrown, pale-tipped dark tail, and vivid chestnut rump, often visible in flight.

name: Varied Solitaire
rangeDescription: Highlands of far eastern panama (darién) and adjacent northwestern colombia
description: Medium-sized thrush with extremely limited range at the border of Panama and Colombia. Unlikely to be mistaken—gray head and underparts with black face and brown back are unique.

name: White-browed Guan
rangeDescription: Interior northeastern brazil (ceará and paraíba to bahia)
description: Large, quite uniformly dark brown guan with a broad, bold white eyebrow and prominent white streaks on the upperwing and breast. Occurs in dry forests, where it mostly forages on the ground, sometimes in large groups.

name: Blue-headed Quail-Dove
rangeDescription: Lowlands of cuba (in danger of extinction)
description: A shy plump dove of forests with closed canopies, open understory, and leaf litter. Typically found on the ground and often in pairs.

name: Great Snipe
rangeDescription: Breeds northern palearctic region; winters sub-saharan africa
description: Slightly bigger and stockier than Common Snipe, with a long and thick bill, heavily barred belly and contrasting upperwing pattern with dark underwings. Flushes at close range; escape flight is usually slow and short.

name: Multicolored Tanager
rangeDescription: Locally in andes of western colombia
description: Small stunning tanager with unbelievable color pattern: electric cerulean breast and flanks, black belly, green nape and wings, creamy back, golden face and throat, and black and chestnut ear patch. Sexes similar; females and young birds look duller than males.

name: Yellow-rumped Serin
rangeDescription: Savanna of eritrea and northern ethiopia
description: A very plain gray-brown seedeater with a white throat and a yellow rump that is conspicuous in flight. Found locally in savanna, woodland, and cultivated areas, usually in small flocks.

name: Mountain Pipit
rangeDescription: South africa (drakensberg mountains of southern lesotho)
description: A large, dark, boldly marked pipit with a pinkish base to the bill. Pairs breed in alpine scrub and grassland above 2000 meters of elevation from October to April, before dispersing to wintering grounds presumed to be in Central Africa.

name: Mountain Barbet
rangeDescription: Mountains of northern borneo
description: Faded-looking barbet of Borneo’s north-central mountain ranges. Grass-green above and pale green below, with a pale blue head, an off-white throat, and a bright red streak on the back of the head.
